slides.title: VISA: A Structured Description Protocol for Agent-Based Simulation Models Towards Machine Reproducibility
slides.tldr: STRUCTURED PROTOCOL FOR MACHINE-REPRODUCIBLE AGENT-BASED MODELS
slides.highlight: VISA introduces a symbol-based description protocol and LLM-executable skills to make agent-based models machine-parseable and reproducible, supporting the agent-based simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: VISA is a symbol-based, table-driven protocol designed to make agent-based models machine-reproducible and unambiguous.
card.key_idea: A structured protocol using eight interconnected tables (four agent-level, four model-level) and nineteen consistency rules to enable automated parsing and LLM-assisted code generation.
card.evaluation: Validated on three external ABMs; successfully reproduced two cross-language (NetLogo to Python) and captured one industrial AnyLogic model, identifying specific proprietary blockers.
card.limitation: Reproduction can be blocked by proprietary libraries or unavailable data, which the protocol identifies but cannot bypass.

slides.title: Cocktail-Talker: Multi-Speaker Dialog Modeling in Noisy Social Environments with Turn Action GRPO
slides.tldr: MULTI-SPEAKER DIALOG MODELING IN NOISY ENVIRONMENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a speech LLM framework that uses action tokens to decide whether to respond, listen, or ignore in multi-speaker social settings, aligning with HyECHO's focus on addressee modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: Cocktail-Talker enables speech assistants to selectively respond, listen, or ignore in noisy multi-speaker social environments.
card.key_idea: A Qwen2.5-Omni-based framework using three action tokens, trained via SFT and GRPO reinforcement learning on simulated data from the Cocktail-DialogGen pipeline.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on seen/unseen environments using binary Respond/Silent accuracy and response quality metrics (METEOR, ROUGE-L); outperformed baselines like Qwen3-Omni.
card.limitation: The system is not streaming, assumes fixed turn boundaries, and lacks visual or spatial sensors for speaker inference.

slides.title: Belief-Aware Influence and Trust (BAIT): Shaping Human Belief During Repeated Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING HUMAN TRUST IN REPEATED HRI
slides.highlight: The BAIT controller manages the trade-off between long-term influence and human trust during repeated interactions, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: BAIT balances long-term human influence with behavioral transparency to maintain task performance and user trust.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical particle filter tracks fast strategic shifts and slow belief updates, feeding a belief-aware MPPI planner that optimizes the influence-trust trade-off.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via CARLO simulations, a human-subject study, and real-world GEM vehicle lane-merging; compared against Stackelberg and Belief-Entropy baselines.
card.limitation: The approach relies on a structured human model and specific latent state assumptions to ensure real-time computational tractability.

slides.title: Not Forgotten: Implementation and Evaluation of a Personalized Episodic Memory for the Humanoid Robot Head Kim
slides.tldr: EPISODIC MEMORY ENHANCES SOCIAL ROBOT PERCEPTION
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that integrating a personalized episodic memory module into a humanoid robot head increases perceived sociability, trustworthiness, and warmth. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Episodic memory in a humanoid robot head significantly increases perceived sociability without increasing user disturbance.
card.key_idea: A lightweight module using vector-based semantic retrieval and a hybrid scoring function (combining cosine similarity, recency, access frequency, and emotional intensity) to inject personalized context into LLM prompts.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects video-based study (N=43) using the HRIES scale. Results showed significant gains in trustworthiness (d=0.62) and warmth (d=0.56), with no increase in disturbance (d=0.00).
card.limitation: Video-based format lacked real-time interaction; the small student sample and lack of longitudinal data limit generalizability and ecological validity.

slides.title: Teachy Mini: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Knowledge-Based Generative Social Robot for Higher Education
slides.tldr: KNOWLEDGE-BASED GENERATIVE SOCIAL ROBOT FOR TUTORING
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how knowledge-based design and retrieval-augmented generation can create responsible tutoring behavior in social robots, supporting the RwB focus on AI-mediated embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Teachy Mini is a generative social robot using knowledge-based design to provide responsible, personalized higher education tutoring.
card.key_idea: Operationalizes knowledge-based design via system prompting, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for lecture slides, and stateful prompt orchestration to adapt to learner states and preferences.
card.evaluation: Between-subjects study (N=24) comparing KBD vs. control. Teachy Mini was perceived as significantly more responsible, though other metrics showed no significant differences.
card.limitation: Preliminary evaluation with a small sample size (N=24) and limited to a single-session interaction context.

slides.title: Teachers Decry Plan for Humanoid Robot in New York High School
slides.highlight: This report on teacher opposition to humanoid robots in schools provides critical context for RwB regarding the social acceptance of embodied AI in educational settings.

slides.title: Italian Startup Debuts Gene.01 Humanoid With Skin That Senses Humans Before Contact
slides.highlight: The Gene.01 humanoid features skin capable of sensing humans before contact, offering potential advancements for human-robot interaction in RwB.

slides.title: DuplexGen: Adaptive Synthesis of Human-AI Turn-Taking Dialogues
slides.highlight: This work introduces DuplexGen to generate dialogues with turn-taking behaviors calibrated to human preferences across different scenarios, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

slides.title: Do Visual Features Improve Other-Initiated Repair Detection? A Dyadic Multimodal Approach
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that incorporating visual features like gaze and gestures improves the detection of other-initiated repairs, supporting HyECHO's goal of multimodal social perception for communication breakdowns.

card.one_liner: Visual features improve the detection and classification of other-initiated repairs in multimodal conversational dialogue.
card.key_idea: A multimodal model integrating text, audio, and CA-grounded visual features (gaze, facial expressions, posture, gestures) extracted via OpenFace and MediaPipe.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NOXI (French) and CABB-S (Dutch) corpora using macro-F1; TriModal outperformed text-audio baselines and zero-shot Qwen2.5-Omni-7B.
card.limitation: High class imbalance in corpora leads to high variance in results, particularly for rare repair types in NOXI.
